subject: Nanotechnology
title: Block Copolymer Assembly
description: A quick, practical guide to Block Copolymer Assembly.

hook.text: Join two incompatible polymers into one chain and they phase-separate at the nanoscale — creating beautiful patterns.

buildup.text: Block copolymers microphase-separate into spheres, cylinders, lamellae, or bicontinuous networks depending on composition.

discovery.text: The domain size is 5 to 100 nm — perfect for patterning at scales beyond lithography's economic limit.

twist.text: Controlling orientation is the challenge — features naturally form in random directions without external guidance.

climax.text: Intel and Samsung explored block copolymer lithography for sub-10 nm chip features — self-assembly meets semiconductors.

punchline.text: Two polymers that hate each other create patterns no machine can match.

quiz.question: Why are block copolymers useful for nanoscale patterning?
options: They dissolve into individual atoms when heated
Their phase separation creates regular nanoscale patterns at sizes difficult for traditional lithography
They permanently bond to any surface on contact
